headline: Nginx and Java RCE flaws under active probing; AI tooling and supply-chain hijacks
overview: Attackers are scanning for the Java4Shell bug and new critical Nginx HTTP/2 flaws, with patches rushed out by several vendors. A Microsoft AI agent package on PyPI was briefly hijacked to steal cloud credentials, and recent outages have sparked debate about federal staffing and response.

topStories.title: Nginx HTTP/2 and F5 critical flaws demand urgent patching
topStories.summary: F5 issued out-of-band fixes for 22 vulnerabilities, including five critical Nginx bugs, one dating back to 2015. Public proof-of-concept code exists for one HTTP/2 flaw, and researchers chained the Nginx issues with a Linux kernel bug to reach root from inside a container.

topStories.title: Java4Shell probing begins across the internet
topStories.summary: Threat actors have started scanning for the critical Java memory corruption bug that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Vendors including Cisco, Atlassian, Red Hat and others have confirmed affected products, with some patches still in development.

topStories.title: Malware hijacks Microsoft's agent framework package
topStories.summary: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent framework on PyPI carried a credential stealer that ran at Python startup and targeted Azure and CI credentials. Both releases were quarantined; affected users are advised to rebuild environments from clean version 1.26.0 and rotate credentials.

topStories.title: Vendor breaches and data exposures hit major organisations
topStories.summary: JP Morgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard are investigating vendor-linked breaches claimed by the NON extortion group. KPMG Canada confirmed unauthorised access to client tax documents, and SBC Medical Group reported data on about 1.6 million people exposed.

topStories.title: Federal response to infrastructure outages questioned
topStories.summary: Lawmakers and experts questioned whether staffing cuts at CISA and the National Security Council hindered the response to outages that grounded air traffic and disrupted banking and an NSA classified network. The White House says CISA remains equipped and there is no evidence of foreign attack.

topStories.title: AI tooling and exposed AI infrastructure
topStories.summary: Rapid7 found thousands of exposed self-hosted AI servers, many already tampered with by outsiders and some abusing owners' paid cloud models. Separately, a Ukraine-FBI operation arrested four suspects tied to a ransomware ring that used AI-generated voices to steal credentials; Microsoft is testing a stricter Edge lockdown mode.

episodes.title: Four flaws, no time to stall.
episodes.summary: Covers CISA adding four exploited flaws to its catalog, the Java4Shell probing, the Nginx and Splunk patch wave, and a Ukrainian ransomware arrest. Also features a sponsored-style interview with Russell Van Tyle of SpectorOps on using AI in offensive security via the Sage research project.

episodes.title: Credit giants follow the vendor trail, European Commission systems take sick leave, SBC loses 1.6M customers' data
episodes.summary: Reports on vendor breaches affecting Chase, Visa and Mastercard, European Commission systems disrupted for over ten days, a Cisco Expressway root-command flaw, and a malicious Microsoft agent package on PyPI. Also covers SBC Medical data exposure and a Transport for London photocard incident.

episodes.title: Honeypot Analysis as Code; PHP Patches and Session RCE (CVE-2026-126714); Dragos AI Canary Tokens; vCenter Exploit (CVE-2026-123890) (Nov 20th 2026)
episodes.summary: Covers PHP security patches including a session-handling remote code execution issue, Canary token research showing AI providers and proxies leaking data, and a note on a vSphere flaw already being exploited.

episodes.title: CST F5 Patches 11-Year-Old NGINX Flaw, Malware Hits Microsoft Agent Framework
episodes.summary: Covers the Nginx flaws including the 2015 bug and the Linux kernel chain, the hijacked Microsoft agent toolkit, the KPMG Canada client data breach, and attempts to exploit Java4Shell along with firewall mitigation options.

episodes.title: The 10 Biggest Days in AI History
episodes.summary: A retrospective on the ten biggest days in AI history, timed to the Anthropic IPO, covering milestones from OpenAI's founding through agentic AI, government clashes and the November midterms. Not a cyber news episode.

episodes.title: Inside China’s new AI propaganda machine: The GoLaxy papers
episodes.summary: Notes describe a discussion of leaked documents about a Chinese company running AI-generated personas for information operations, but the supplied text is only a short description, so details beyond that are not available.

episodes.title: MiTM Emulated Android Apps, Keep Calm And Carry On - PSW #953
episodes.summary: Covers a technical segment on using Waydroid and mitmproxy to intercept Android apps, plus a long list of security news items including AI-assisted pentesting, router and flight disruptions, and script-tag skimmers. Details beyond the topic list are not in the notes.

episodes.title: NGINX HTTP/2 RCE, F5 BIG-IP Critical Flaws, and a Hijacked Microsoft Package
episodes.summary: Covers the critical Nginx HTTP/2 flaws, six critical F5 BIG-IP flaws, the hijacked Microsoft PyPI package, an exploited Apache Roller flaw, and the Chrome 158 patch release, along with ransomware arrests and a Palo Alto acquisition.

episodes.title: nginx RCE flaws, UPS software hijacks a domain controller | Cyber Security News Nov 19
episodes.summary: Covers public exploit code for Nginx flaws, a UPS management software flaw used to reach a domain controller, LiteLLM and Apache Roller exploitation, a Redcap flaw, persistent router botnets, a Windows Hello and BitLocker PIN weakness, and an extortion-linked supplier breach.
